newsitem.title: UK: Quiet Brady bonds focus on Bulgaria, Russia.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Brady bonds focus on Bulgaria, Russia.

text.p: Trading of emerging market debt in Europe on Monday was limited, although Bulgarian and Russian paper did strengthen.

"The market is very quiet, but the bid for Bulgaria and Russia is a bit stronger," a trader at a U.S. bank said, adding the price rises were due to client demand rather than changes in their fundamentals.
"We will be very heavily dependent this week on U.S. data. The market is up for now but may change depending what happens to U.S. Treasuries," he said.
Bulgarian FRBs were quoted at 46-1/4 bid, 1/2 up.
Russian dollar Vnesh bonds were bid at 79.00, up 1/4. The biggest gain in the MinFin sector was on MinFin series 6, bid of 47-5/8, up 5/8.
A batch of important U.S. data will be released this week, which will be closely watched for signs of inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy.
On Monday a report on new hone sales will be released. On Tuesday the first quarter Employment Cost Index and April consumer confidence figures surface.
On Wednesday, gross domestic product (GDP) for the first quarter is released. The April NAPM report comes on Thursday, and on Friday the all-important employment report for April will hit the market.
On May 20 the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets and could raise U.S. interest rates.
"The focus in very much on Treasuries, because any move there could shock the Brady market," a dealer at a European banks said.
U.S. Treasuries held steady in London on Monday. Even the dollar's rise to its highest level since August 1994 after a weekend Group of Seven (G7) meeting failed to boost the sector, dealers said.
